newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sakakibara says foreigners buying yen since Feb 20.
newsitem.headline: Sakakibara says foreigners buying yen since Feb 20.

text.p: Foreigners have been buying the yen since February 20 and foreign exchange rates have been relatively stable after the Group of Seven (G7) industrialised nations' meeting earlier this month, Eisuke Sakakibara, a senior Japanese Finance Ministry official, said on Friday.

"It was acknowledged at the G7 meeting that the correction of the strong yen from last year has ended. The forex market following the G7 meeting has been rather stable," said Sakakibara, director-general of the ministry's International Finance Bureau.
On movements in Thursday's forex market, he said: "Foreigners have been buying the yen."
Sakakibara said exchange rates had moved recently, mainly on the interest rate differential between the United States and Japan. He added that the yen had strengthened a bit in the last few days.

"The forex rate is moving on the rate gap between the U.S. and Japan. Although views are mixed over the economic outlooks of the two nations, the yen has strengthened a bit in the past two, three days," Sakakibara said.
